Permutations

Source: R/combinatorics-permgroups.R
Permutation.Rd

Permutation() builds a permutation of 0..n-1, following SymPy's constructor: an integer vector of length two or more is the array form (Permutation(c(2, 0, 1))), a list gives disjoint or composed cycles (Permutation(list(c(0, 1), c(2, 3)))), several integers form one cycle (Permutation(1, 2)), a single integer n is the identity on 0..n (Permutation(3)), and no argument is the empty permutation. size pads with fixed points and must be named. * composes (p * q applies p first, then q), ^ with a number is a power, p ^ q with a permutation is the conjugate q^-1 p q, i ^ p is the image of the integer i, and p + k or p - k move k steps in lexicographic rank.

perm_call(p, ...)

perm_next_lex(p)

Arguments

...

For Permutation(), the array form, a list of cycles, integers forming one cycle, a Permutation or a Cycle. For perm_call(), an index, a vector to permute, or integers of a cycle to multiply by. For perm_rmul(), permutations.

size

Total size; pads with fixed points.

p, q

Permutations.

i

An element or vector of elements.

perms

A list of permutations.

x

A character string (its characters) or a vector.

key

An optional function mapping each element to its sort key.

n

A size.

r

A rank.

m, s

Josephus parameters: every mth of n is removed until s remain.

inversion

An inversion vector.

Value

A Permutation, an integer, logical, vector or list.

Details

The helpers mirror the methods of SymPy's Permutation: array_form(), cyclic_form(), full_cyclic_form(), perm_size(), perm_list(), perm_support(), perm_inverse(), apply_perm(), perm_call(), perm_rmul(), perm_prod(), perm_mul_inv(), perm_commutes_with(), perm_commutator(), perm_transpositions(), perm_atoms(), perm_order(), perm_parity(), perm_sign(), perm_signature(), perm_is_even(), perm_is_odd(), perm_is_identity(), perm_is_singleton(), perm_is_empty(), perm_cycle_structure(), perm_cycles(), perm_length(), perm_max(), perm_min(), perm_ascents(), perm_descents(), perm_runs(), perm_index(), perm_inversions(), perm_inversion_vector(), perm_cardinality(), perm_resize().

Examples

p <- Permutation(c(1, 2, 0))
q <- Permutation(list(c(0, 1)), size = 3)
p * q
#> (1 2)
perm_order(p)
#> [1] 3
cyclic_form(p * q)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 1 2
#> 
Permutation(1, 2, size = 4)
#> (3)(1 2)
